alignments.note: Finite verb with its supplied subject pronoun, headed on the lexical verb (rules 7, 9).
Connective particle rendered *Yea*.
Noun.
Attributive adjective.
Connective.

One Greek compound adjective rendered by *grievous to be borne*, both English words glossing an element: *grievous* answers to the privative-force prefix δυσ- and *borne* to the verbal core βαστ-. Rule 66's compound clause heads such a unit on the core and not on the prefixed element, even where English syntax makes the modifier the phrase's formal head, and rule 104 records the identical shape in εὐπειθής → *easy to be entreated* headed on *entreated* and εὐάρεστος → *well pleasing* headed on its stem word. Heading on *grievous* would head the prefix.
Connective.
Finite verb with its supplied object pronoun as a rule 7 helper on the verb that requires it in English (rule 74).
Preposition.
Determiner slot taken by the possessive *men's*, which belongs to ἀνθρώπων (rules 20, 57).
Noun, bare after the displacing possessive.
The English possessor *men's* carries no determiner of its own, so the inner article anchors nothing (rules 23, 57).
Genitive noun rendered with *'s*.
Intensive αὐτός rendered by a two-word English emphatic, headed on the *-self* word (rule 107); the plain *they* is the subject word English syntax requires.
Adversative particle.
Determiner slot taken by *their*, which belongs to αὐτῶν (rule 20).
With the determiner displaced, the case preposition *with* stays with the noun (rule 20), discontinuously under rule 15.
Genitive pronoun carries the possessive.
Ordinary negative to *not*; no negative indefinite competes for it.
θέλω rendered by the modal *will*.
Infinitive; the ASV writes no infinitival marker after the modal.
Accusative pronoun.

review_notes: Corrected the head of δυσβάστακτα → *grievous to be borne* from *grievous* to *borne*: rule 66 heads a compound rendered by two glossing English words on the verbal core, and rule 104's εὐπειθής → *easy to be entreated* is the same shape. Edges and all other units unchanged.
The projection carries r01 with δυσβάστακτα, which the ASV translates; the ASV's own note records the shorter reading, but the English is aligned to the token present (rule 12).

*men's* treated as a genitive possessor displacing the outer article's determiner under rule 20's *'s* clause, with the inner article unrepresented for want of a determiner on the possessor (rule 57).
